Score the test rows one time

Source: R/score.R
evaluate_once.Rd

Runs decide() with a setup on the test rows and scores them as score_setup() does, but only once. It writes the result to path, and it refuses to run again while path exists, so the test rows are not tuned against.

Usage

evaluate_once(setup, text = NULL, image = NULL, truth, event = NULL, path)

Arguments

setup

A setup from decision_setup() or read_setup() with one question.

text, image

The inputs, as in decide().

truth

A factor or character vector with the true answer of each input. It has the length of the inputs, and its values are answers of the question.

event

The answer that counts as the event (the positive class) of the AUC. NULL (the default) gives "true" for a noul question and the second answer for a question with two answers (for c(normal = ..., defective = ...), "defective"). With three or more answers, event is required.

path

The path of the result file (an .rds file in a folder that exists). If it exists, evaluate_once() stops before any request.

Value

The one-row tibble of score_setup(). It is also written to path with saveRDS() when no row has an error. While a row has an error, estimate is NA: the estimate appears only in the complete result.

Details

decide() keeps its state in paste0(path, ".state.json"). A run that stops continues from this file without paying twice, and each test row is scored once. When a row has an error, evaluate_once() returns the row with estimate = NA, does not write path, and warns with the failed rows that a new call sends only them again. So the test rows give one estimate only, and you cannot tune on them by repeated calls.

A test row can fail at each call, for example with an image that the provider refuses. Then the estimate cannot appear until that row has an answer or leaves the test rows. Read the reason in the .error column of answers. If a new call cannot fix the row, remove it from the test rows, call evaluate_once() again with the same path, and report the removed row with the result. The state file keeps the other answers, so they are not sent again.

See also

score_setup() for the tuning rows, and decision_setup() to make a setup.

Other scoring: score_setup()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs an API key and makes paid calls, so it is not run on CRAN.
quality <- question_choice("Is the part defective?", c(
  nominal = "A clean part.", defective = "A part with a defect."
))
setup <- decision_setup(decider_typesafe("jev-1.13.0"), list(q = quality))
test_texts <- c("Clean surface.", "Dark streak.")
test_truth <- c("nominal", "defective")
evaluate_once(
  setup, text = test_texts, truth = test_truth,
  path = tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
)
} # }
